input.rationale:
Section 1.4 (p0008-p0009) is the only inbound grant to us (the sole express licence, in Section 6.1/p0038, runs from us to HDI on our Marks and so benefits our party). The 1.4 grant is not stated to be revocable at HDI's discretion, which is positive, but it names only "the Company": neither our affiliates nor contractors acting on our behalf are covered, and there is no notice-based mechanism to add them. That fails the fallback's affiliate prong and approaches the walk-away description (affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them); the successor point is only partly covered by the general assignment provision in Section 10.3. Redline adds affiliates and contractors, confirms exercise by a successor, and confirms the rights are not revocable other than on termination under Section 4 — the smallest edit reaching the preferred position.</parationale>

proposal.summary: Extend the Section 1.4 access and use rights to the Company's affiliates and contractors, confirm transfer to a successor, and confirm the rights are not revocable at HDI's discretion.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the Section 1.4 access and use rights to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, since our group and our service providers operate the Site day to day, and confirmed the rights pass to a successor and are not revocable at HDI's discretion before termination under Section 4. If helpful, we can accept affiliate coverage on written notice to HDI as a fallback.

ops.newText: HDI shall also provide the Company with access to HDI's software and Content administration tools for purposes of allowing the Company to monitor current catalog information. The access and use rights granted to the Company under this Section 1.4 extend to the Company's affiliates and to contractors acting on the Company's behalf, may be exercised by any successor to the Company's business (including in a merger or acquisition), and shall not be suspended or revoked by HDI except upon termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 4.
